function: Joint downlink pilot design, channel estimation and CSI feedback (compression and reconstruction) with a Swin Transformer network, SWTCAN (p. 2).
system: BS with 16x16 UPA (256 antennas), single-antenna UEs, FDD, OFDM with 256 subcarriers, 28 GHz; no RIS (p. 2; p. 4).
method: Swin Transformer autoencoder trained end-to-end on NMSE; VAE sample generator for pre-training; federated fine-tuning (FedAMS) over the air of about 11% of parameters (p. 3).
data_channel: Sionna-generated 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-A, CDL-B, CDL-C channels; 6000 training, 2000 validation, 2000 test samples; no measured data (p. 4).
test_conditions: Pre-train on 6000 CDL-A samples, adapt with 120 CDL-B, test on 2000 CDL-B; federated tuning: 600 UEs, 10 CSI samples each (p. 5; p. 6).
baselines: Transformer CE plus Transformer feedback [18]; MMV-LAMP CE with CsiNet or Transformer feedback; perfect-CE and perfect-feedback oracles; centralized learning versus federated tuning (p. 4; p. 6).
metrics: NMSE versus feedback bits; pre-training test NMSE; NMSE versus uplink communication overhead; FLOPs and complexity order (p. 4; p. 5; p. 6).
complexity: Complexity orders: SWTCAN 1.4e7, Transformer 1.5e8, MMV-LAMP 1.1e10, CsiNet 2.4e6; FLOPs in Table II; 32.6M and 3.6M parameters (p. 5; p. 6).
openness: Code released at https://github.com/BIT-ZY/CSI-GPT (p. 1); channels generated with the Sionna library (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "where the CDL channel models are adopted from 3GPP standards [20]"; ref. [20] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 7); training and test data are Sionna CDL-A/B/C.
q2_support: p. 5: "We pre-train SWTCAN with 6000 CDL-A samples, fine-tune it with 120 CDL-B samples" and "tested on 2000 CDL-B samples": pretrained on another CDL profile, adapted with few new samples.
q3_support: p. 4: "Baseline 1: The Transformer-based network for CE and CSI feedback [18]" is learned, but no non-learned estimator (LS, MMSE, OMP) is compared; MMV-LAMP and CsiNet are learned, perfect CE and feedback are oracles, CL versus federated (p. 6) is a variant of the method.
q4_support: p. 5: "we have analyzed the complexity of the proposed algorithm and the baselines": order about 1.4e7 for SWTCAN, with the baseline orders; p. 6, Table II lists computation cost in FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 1: "Our code is publicly available at" https://github.com/BIT-ZY/CSI-GPT
notes: Area 2: the learned function is joint pilot design, CE and CSI feedback (p. 2); AirComp federated tuning only fine-tunes this estimator, so area 7 does not apply (p. 3-4). q3 is 0 because every baseline is learned (MMV-LAMP is a learned unfolded estimator, p. 4) or an oracle (perfect CE or feedback); if the reviewer counts the perfect-CE oracle as non-learned, q3 changes. The arXiv v2 text includes a pasted reply to reviewers on p. 4 (CDL-A and CDL-C results of Fig. 3); not used for the marks. The paper says SWTCAN has lower complexity than the baselines, but its CsiNet figure (2.4e6) is below that of SWTCAN (1.4e7) (p. 5).
